description: Figure 4 illustrates the number of participants who identified each evaluation criterion as beneficial. The horizontal axis displays the evaluation criteria, labeled “Multilingual TEMs outperform English TEMs,” “Filtration with LLMs improves precision but has trade-offs,” “Base LLMs excel in summarization and veracity prediction,” and “Smaller LLMs often failed to perform language-independent veracity checks,” listed in that order. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of participants (N=6)”, presents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 6, with tick marks at intervals of 1.  Four bars are displayed, each corresponding to one of the evaluation criteria. The bar for “Multilingual TEMs outperform English TEMs” is light blue and extends to a value of 5. The bar for “Filtration with LLMs improves precision but has trade-offs” is light blue and extends to a value of 4. The bar for “Base LLMs excel in summarization and veracity prediction” is light blue and extends to a value of 3. Finally, the bar for “Smaller LLMs often failed to perform language-independent veracity checks” is light blue and extends to a value of 2. The bars are not sorted and are all the same color.
